sites.name: Lusion (studio site, v3)
sites.award: Awwwards Site of the Year 2023. Older than the 2024–2026 window, but still live and still the benchmark 3D agency homepage. Lusion also won SOTM Apr 2026 with Oryzo (below).
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: the hero is not full-bleed. It is a rounded-corner canvas card inset on a pale lavender-grey page. Inside it, a dense pile of glossy plastic pipe-joint or cross-shaped solids (cobalt blue, white, black) tumbles and collides under studio lighting, like a physics simulation. As you scroll, the card moves up as part of the page and reveals a huge 'Bold Ideas, Brought to Life' headline, with a small blue 3D figure peeking in. Next comes a 'PLAY REEL' section, where a rounded video card grows to fill the frame (it showed a red slab of phone mockups at one point), then a two-column Featured Work grid. The loader is a pixel 'L' with a 000→100 counter.
techniques: Three.js real-time PBR glossy plastic with an environment map
Rigid-body or physics-style stacking and collisions of many instances
Canvas kept in a framed DOM card, not a fixed full-screen layer
sites.palette_and_type: Pale lavender-grey page, cobalt/ultramarine blue as the only chromatic accent, plus black and white solids. Large neutral grotesk display type with tiny uppercase micro-labels ('SCROLL TO EXPLORE', '+' crop marks).
sites.scroll_choreography: The 3D sits in its own card. The page does not scroll-jack: normal document flow moves the card away, and the 3D stays an object on display rather than the whole environment.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Observed at 375px: the headline moves above the canvas, and the canvas becomes a tall portrait rounded card. The full 3D physics pile still runs, reframed vertically. No horizontal layout tricks.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Put ProDevly's totems in a framed 'vitrine' card (rounded rect with crop marks) instead of a full-bleed void. The page stays readable, the 3D feels like a curated sculpture, and on mobile the card switches to portrait, which fixes the 'everything on the left' problem from tour-travel-3d.

sites.name: Oryzo AI
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 13 Apr 2026 + Developer Award; Site of the Month April 2026
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: the loader is an orange CAD-style reticle on olive green. The hero is a photoreal top-down desk (green cutting mat, ruler, pencil) with a cork coaster and a big 'ORYZO' wordmark. Scrolling performs a 3D→2D→3D transition (Awwwards lists this element by name). The coaster lifts out of the desk 'photo' onto a near-black stage under warm raking light, stays pinned at centre, and rotates from top-down to edge-on as you scroll. Copy ('ISN'T JUST A COASTER.') sits on either side of it. There are also WebGL sketch interactions and interactive particles in the footer.
techniques: Scroll-pinned single hero object, with scroll mapped to rotation and tilt
Camera moves through Z depth rather than sliding 2D layers (per the Utsubo review)
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #100904 (warm black) and #FF8539 (orange). Off-white condensed uppercase grotesk headlines, small sans body.
sites.scroll_choreography: One object, many scroll beats. The object's pose changes per beat while the text blocks swap around it. The camera never travels far.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Observed at 375px: the coaster stays centred and grows to almost full width. Copy stacks above and below it instead of beside it. The hero keeps the desk plate with the wordmark on top and a video-thumbnail card at the bottom.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Give each section exactly ONE pinned totem whose pose (rotation, tilt, assembly) is driven by damped scroll progress, not by position along a path. On mobile, put copy above and below the centred object. This avoids the 'car too fast to follow' problem because the object never translates across the screen.

sites.name: Igloo Inc.
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 23 Jul 2024 (Animations/Transitions 9.6), SOTM Jul 2024, Site of the Year 2024
sites.what_3d_does: From the Awwwards case study: a three-section landing page for the parent company of Pudgy Penguins. Each portfolio company is an object encased in its own ice block. The ice is grown with a custom procedural crystal-growth algorithm, so every block is different. In the links section, a particle simulation swirls and re-forms into a different shape for each hovered link, and particles change colour with speed and glow. The intro is a real-time in-engine animation that flows straight into the experience. The camera travels to a particle effect in the footer. Transitions combine chromatic aberration, 'tech displacement' and a frost effect. (In our headless browser pane the page stayed on its loader, so this is not observed directly.)
techniques: VDB volumes converted to a compressed custom format
UI text rendered in WebGL with SDF fonts, with glitch and scramble done by shader
In-browser tools for live shader and texture editing
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #b6bac5 and #383e4e, a cold blue-grey duotone. Monospace-style UI text rendered in WebGL.
sites.scroll_choreography: Only three sections, so scroll stays engaging by moving from object to object (ice blocks) and then into a particle finale in the footer.
sites.mobile_behaviour: The case study says performance was measured continuously and tuned for low-end devices, with textures and shaders loaded in the background. Awwwards Responsive score 8.4. Not verified on a device.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Give every service or project its own unique material 'capsule' (resin, glass, ceramic) generated procedurally from one base, so the 3D carries identity for each item. Keep the homepage short (few sections) and make each one richer.

sites.name: Lando Norris
sites.award: Awwwards Site of the Year 2025 + Users' Choice
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: the hero is a full-bleed portrait on off-white with faint topographic contour lines. A 3D helmet layer sits over his head, and the cursor paints or reveals it, so the helmet appears through a mask that follows the mouse. Scrolling switches to a dark olive section with giant mixed serif/condensed headlines and a neon-lime signature that draws itself over a portrait card. After that comes a scattered collage of photos and video at different depths, moving at different parallax speeds.
techniques: WebGL cursor mask reveal of a 3D helmet over a photo
Reactive blob overlays derived from his helmet graphics (per DesignRush)
Modular On Track / Off Track content
sites.palette_and_type: #CBF902 acid lime, #2D3126 olive-black, #F4F3F1 off-white, #7F8177 grey (per DesignRush). Mix of a high-contrast serif and a heavy condensed sans in all caps.
sites.scroll_choreography: Light hero → dark statement band with an animated signature → free-floating collage. The colour mode flips between sections.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Use ProDevly's own brand mark (logo glyph or a '</>'-style stroke) as a drawn stroke and as the reveal mask over the hero totem. Note how a single acid accent on a muted base reads as more 'colourful' and premium than a rainbow.

sites.name: Messenger
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 10 Nov 2025 (Dev 8.21, Animations 9.0, WPO 8.8); Developer Site of the Year 2025
sites.what_3d_does: A tiny cel/toon-shaded planet. You play a third-person character who walks around the sphere delivering mail. The camera follows over the curved horizon. It has live multiplayer over WebSockets (you see other players and their 3D emoji), NPCs, and character customisation for hair and clothes.
techniques: Houdini + Blender assets (per one secondary write-up, unverified)
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #81BFBC (soft teal) and #C9D5C3 (sage). Pastel, matte, solid forms.
sites.scroll_choreography: Not scroll-driven: character-driven navigation in a contained diorama.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Reported to run smoothly on desktop and mobile. Awwwards Responsive 8.4.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Colourful does not have to mean neon gradients. Matte, solid, toon-lit forms in a controlled pastel set look like real sculpted totems. A small, contained diorama also suits mobile, because the camera never travels long distances.

sites.name: Immersive Garden (studio site)
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 7 Jan 2025 (8.0), SOTM Jan 2025; Immersive Garden is Agency of the Year in the same annual results that name Lando Norris SOTY 2025
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: after a counter loader, the hero is a light-grey plaster wall with sculpted bas-relief flowers rising out of the surface, plus a small serif line, 'Innovative digital experiences studio'. As you scroll, more relief sculptures (birds, hands) slide past, and a project video appears framed inside a 3D architectural interior (columns, planters). Later project tiles appear as objects on the grey ground. Awwwards highlights: 'Bas-relief' interaction, 'Rapid Scroll' feature, menu transition.
techniques: Relief and displacement sculpture lit in real time
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #000000 and #c2c2c2: fully monochrome plaster grey. A small, elegant serif with tiny UI labels.
sites.scroll_choreography: Sculpture → room → project objects, all on one continuous material surface.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Sculpture as a material: totems could rise out of a coloured clay or plaster ground plane rather than float in a void, with the cursor acting as a moving light that rakes across the relief.

sites.name: Terminal Industries
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 3 Sep 2025 + Dev Award; Business & Services Honors Aug 2025; SOTM Sep 2025
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: the hero is a cinematic photoreal semi-truck at dusk. On scroll it turns into a glowing wireframe 'digital twin' of the truck floating in a black star-field, matching what the product does (a yard operating system that digitises physical assets). Later light-theme sections use rounded cards ('#1 Fast start / #2 Single site / #3 Enterprise') and an interactive ROI calculator that works out savings from the visitor's own inputs.
techniques: Interactive calculator in place of marketing stats
sites.palette_and_type: Warm dusk photography → pure black with cyan-white lines → light grey UI cards. Clean grotesk with monospace numbered labels.
sites.scroll_choreography: Physical → digital → product UI, one transformation per beat.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: The 'physical → digital' morph is the natural story for a dev company: a solid, colourful totem dissolves into wireframe or code lines as it enters the 'How we build' section. Show numbers only through interactive tools that compute from the visitor's input (for example a project estimator), never as made-up stats.

sites.name: Cerebrium
sites.studio: KOKI-KIKO / Louis Paquet (3D: Célia Lopez, WebGL: Mathis Biabiany)
sites.what_3d_does: A serverless AI infrastructure SaaS made tangible. A single canvas holds several 3D environments with seamless page transitions and no loading screens between them. A network of glowing paths 'pulses' as the camera flies through it; the paths are static meshes with a UV-scrolling opacity mask and random speed, offset and interval, revealed by distance from the camera. Camera moves are baked from Cinema 4D. The security section is a near-invisible spherical force-field: a Fresnel rim with noise and a hex grid. A raycaster writes cursor hits into a texture that fades over time, so the shield 'remembers' touches. Awwwards also highlights an interactive WebGL globe with force field on scroll, a parallax 3D mask on the About page, and a transparent pricing calculator.
techniques: Started with WebGPURenderer + TSL, then reverted to WebGLRenderer because TSL shader compile took about 20 s at load
EffectComposer with custom passes, tuned bloom
Purple HDRI shared across scenes to unify colour
Draco, with meshes split to keep curves smooth
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #172B76 (navy) and #902177 (magenta). Observed: dark navy UI, hot-pink accent words, ribbed purple 3D forms, monospace terminal UI.
sites.scroll_choreography: Camera flies along baked paths through a network, then each product idea (scaling, security, global regions) gets its own object.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Turn each abstract service (APIs, cloud, security, maintenance) into one tangible, touchable object, such as a security totem with a Fresnel shield that remembers touches. Use one shared environment map so differently coloured totems still feel like one world. Avoid WebGPU-only shader compile times at launch.

sites.name: Shader (Shader Development Studio)
sites.studio: Shader Development Studio (Filip Kantedal, Simon Hedlund)
sites.what_3d_does: A satirical 1980s 'high tech business' world: beige computers, glossy office ads, golden ties, corporate handshakes. Each page section is its own 3D scene, and only scenes in view render. Scenes render in reverse order into FBOs, and each scene receives the next scene's texture. The hero transition flies the camera into a CRT monitor mesh: a frustum-matched plane whose screen already shows the next scene. Other transitions sample the next scene in screen space, for example a handshake into Contact and paper shreds at the end of About revealing what lies beneath. Lenis is modified to snap between Hero and Work.
techniques: Next.js + React Three Fiber + TSL (WebGPU with WebGL compatibility)
Selective rendering from a section-length config
useImperativeHandle render chain instead of per-component useFrame
Post-processing: film grain, chromatic aberration, bloom
sites.palette_and_type: Retro corporate beige, gold and office greys, deliberately degraded 'business brochure' imagery.
sites.scroll_choreography: Scroll moves from scene to scene, and every boundary is a physical 3D portal (monitor screen, shredded paper) rather than a fade.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Not documented. Page lengths adapt to viewport content. The authors admit that UI rendered in canvas hurts accessibility.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: This is the closest stack match (Next.js + R3F). Copy the selective-rendering and FBO-portal architecture, for example a camera that dives into a laptop or IDE screen on a totem to enter 'Our Projects'. Keep all text in the DOM, not in uikit.

sites.name: Trionn
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD Jul 2026 (dated 27 Jul on its own page, 29 Jul in the SOTD listing) and Honorable Mention 23 Jun 2026; also FWA, CSS Design Awards, Orpetron
sites.what_3d_does: From the Codrops case study: the hero is the brand symbol built from separate glass-like panels that idle-rotate, each arm drifting on its own sine phase. Raycast magnetic hover 'charges' the panel under the cursor (envMapIntensity, clearcoat and transmission ramp up, plus a synthesised beep). Holding the mouse for 0.5 s makes the UI vibrate, then the symbol explodes into its panels along predefined vectors, and releasing reverses it. A single explodeAmt value takes the max of scroll, hover and hold, so states blend and reverse cleanly. Hovering the guide lines throws weld sparks between them. Services is one scroll-progress-driven sequence: a 371-frame WebP image sequence, 'OUR SERVICES' glyphs exploding into particles, six cards flying in on curved paths, a palette flip from black to white, then a stripe wipe. A Dribbble gallery bends cards onto a parametric helix that rotates past the camera and unrolls into a flat grid. (In our headless pane the site stayed on its loader.)
techniques: GSAP + ScrollTrigger + SplitText, with Lenis driven by gsap.ticker
Vanilla Three.js rather than R3F, for a single shared render loop
Render-on-scroll with an idle ticker that stops when the scene settles
Reduced motion slows animation rather than killing it
sites.palette_and_type: Pure black and white (per Awwwards). Blur-to-sharp character reveals. DOM headline over the canvas with mix-blend-mode: difference.
sites.scroll_choreography: Pinned sections, each with its own single progress driver. Stripe-wipe transitions are reused between sections for consistency.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Separate gsap.matchMedia animation values and mobile-specific image positions. The services sequence is remapped for mobile.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Same stack (Next.js + Tailwind) and same market. For each totem, build ONE normalised state value (assembled ↔ exploded) fed by damped scroll + hover + press. That gives smooth, reversible and interruptible motion, which fixes the jerky sync seen in tour-travel-3d. Render only when that value changes.

sites.name: PX PUSH
sites.studio: PX PUSH (Lewis Webber / Stud Creative House)
sites.award: Awwwards SOTD 15 Aug 2026 + Developer Award (Animations 8.8, Responsive 8.2)
sites.what_3d_does: A design-subscription studio themed as a 1988 office machine. Three separate Three.js scenes: (1) the logo SVG is extruded with bevels into a mirror-chrome object (metalness + clearcoat, PMREM environment) that shrinks on scroll and travels from the hero centre into the header, where it becomes the home link; its spin follows scroll velocity and reverses with scroll direction. (2) A cloud-flight hero made of about 8,000 cloud planes merged into one geometry, with a shader for edge fade and fog; hovering the word 'speed' speeds the flight up 10×. (3) A floppy-disk GLTF in the pricing section that rotates and tilts with scroll, an on-the-nose take on a 'package'. The founders are 15-angle photo sequences that rotate as you scroll.
techniques: GSAP/ScrollTrigger on one shared clock with Lenis
Page lifecycle registry (prepared → revealed → ready) so the page waits for each scene's first frame
sites.palette_and_type: #03049C (Blue Screen of Death blue) and #BABABA (old Mac plastic grey). Retro corporate type, an oversized marquee title for every section.
sites.scroll_choreography: The logo totem docks into the navbar, and section objects rotate and tilt with progress beside their copy.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Lenis is switched off entirely on mobile in favour of native scroll.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Extrude ProDevly's logo SVG into a coloured lacquer or chrome totem that flies from the hero into the navbar on scroll. Give the pricing section a literal 3D object for the 'package'. Use native scroll on mobile, and do not reveal the page until each canvas has painted its first frame.

sites.name: Shopify Editions (Winter '26 'Renaissance' / Spring '26 'Everywhere')
sites.studio: Shopify Design (Andy Thelander, Damien Mortini, Danetag and others)
sites.award: Renaissance Edition: Awwwards SOTD 9 Feb 2026 (Dev Award 8.05, Animations 9.4), SOTM Feb 2026. Spring '26: Codrops engineering case study, Jun 2026.
sites.what_3d_does: Renaissance: 150+ product updates presented as a mashup of generative paintings and commerce UI, with a hidden layer, intro and hero transitions. Spring '26 (from the case study): one fullscreen canvas behind the DOM with nested FBOs. WebGL handles atmosphere, point clouds, volumetric light and scroll transitions, while the DOM keeps all content. Video is turned into KTX2 array textures and raymarched as soft volumetric light. Point clouds are generated from short videos and packed in a custom compressed format that a worker decodes. A shared fluid field reacts to cursor and scroll velocity. Type scatters and re-forms between depth-layered panels.
techniques: Device tiers 0–3 (0 = static fallback) with DPR clamping
Only the active and adjacent scenes stay mounted
Scroll drives uniforms through refs, not React state
Raymarched KTX2 volumes with capped steps
A designer playground that shares the production preset schema
sites.palette_and_type: Renaissance: #F7F7EE parchment and #292919 near-black, with painterly imagery.
sites.scroll_choreography: Each content section maps to a scene preset (camera, environment, post, mobile offsets, transition), and the app composites between neighbouring scenes.
sites.mobile_behaviour: Mobile is capped hard: smaller point-cloud variants, lower render cost and clamped DPR, with webglcontextlost recovery for iOS Safari.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Mandatory engineering pattern for Next.js: device tiers with a static poster fallback, scroll → uniforms via refs (no re-renders), mount only nearby scenes, and keep every word in the DOM for SEO and accessibility.

sites.name: Phantom (phantom.land)
sites.award: Codrops case study, 30 Jun 2025. Awwwards award not verified in this research.
sites.what_3d_does: The homepage is an infinite project grid. The cursor floats the grid gently in the opposite direction. Dragging zooms the camera out with a custom ease, and releasing lets it slide with inertia. A custom post-processing distortion pass bends it between flat and curved and is tweened during transitions, with a vignette. The team carousel shows each employee's face as about 78,400 particles (280×280), built from just a colour photo and a depth map (two 256px WebPs under 15KB each) captured with RealityScan on iPhone. Particle size follows colour brightness, curl noise keeps them alive, transitions inject noise peaking at the midpoint, and a shader adds depth of field.
techniques: Next.js + React Three Fiber, with a vanilla Three.js class for the grid
sites.palette_and_type: Dark UI with photographic colour from the work thumbnails (not verified in detail).
sites.scroll_choreography: The grid is drag-first; the team section is a scrollable carousel.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: For 'Our Developers', use real depth-map particle portraits of the actual team (cheap: two tiny images per person) instead of stock headshots or avatars. It looks authentic and three-dimensional.

sites.name: Akaru
sites.award: Awwwards Site of the Month April 2024
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: an off-white hero filled by an ultra-condensed black 'AKARU' wordmark, followed by full-width project video tiles. Then comes a dark awards section: a black 3D monolith or obelisk 'trophy' is pinned on the left and turns as you scroll, while a long, real list of awards (with a '(35)' count) scrolls on the right. After that, team photos in the 'Agence' section.
techniques: Pinned 3D object beside a scrolling DOM list
sites.palette_and_type: Off-white and black with neutral greys. Ultra-condensed display wordmark, small grotesk.
sites.scroll_choreography: Typographic hero → video → 3D trophy pinned next to the list → team.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Pin a sculptural totem beside a long HTML list (services, partners, tech stack) and step its rotation or material per list item. The list stays real, indexable text. Any count shown must be a real number.

sites.name: Kriss.ai
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: a big percentage loader on a mauve gradient, then a hero with soft clay-like 3D clouds and an isometric cut-away 'dollhouse' clinic under the headline 'Hi, I'm Kriss.' Scrolling zooms the camera into rooms of the building, and the URL updates per stop (for example /home/overview). Awwwards highlights a zoom transition and hotspot-hover interactions.
sites.palette_and_type: Awwwards lists #D1CACC (mauve-grey) and #0F0F0F. Pastel interiors, bold sans headline.
sites.scroll_choreography: One building, many rooms. Each section is a camera stop inside the same model.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: A single 'studio totem' with floors or rooms (Design, Web, SaaS, Mobile, Maintenance), where scroll moves the camera from stop to stop and each stop has its own URL. One model, one material set, cheap to load.

sites.name: Zentry
sites.award: Awwwards SOTM Aug 2024; Business & Services Honors
sites.what_3d_does: From the Awwwards case study: the team deliberately avoided WebGL to keep the DOM fast. The '3D' portal masks and perspective transitions are built with DOM and CSS. Display headlines use FK Screamer, adapted with Florian Karsten so it holds up under distortion, for clashing-perspective letterforms. The soundtrack evolves as you explore, and a motion system was defined before the visual design.
sites.palette_and_type: Bold, vivid gaming palette (not given exactly in the case study). FK Screamer custom display face.
sites.mobile_behaviour: The case study says animations work across devices with memory-efficient tech (no specifics).
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Not every 3D moment needs WebGL. Do card and portal perspective transitions in CSS 3D (cheap on phones) and spend the WebGL budget only on the hero totems.

sites.name: Bruno Simon portfolio (2025 rebuild)
sites.award: Awwwards SOTM Jan 2026; Portfolio Honors Dec 2025
sites.what_3d_does: A physics-driven car on a stylised, colourful island. Work and Lab items are in-world 3D objects. Wind moves grass and foliage. Weather and day-night cycles are shared live by all visitors, with light multiplayer (messages, counters, leaderboard).
techniques: Three.js WebGPU + TSL with automatic WebGL fallback
Physics bodies generated from Blender naming conventions
About 78,400 single-triangle grass blades in one geometry
ONE palette texture that every model samples by UV
sites.palette_and_type: Bright toy-like nature colours, all taken from a single palette texture.
sites.mobile_behaviour: An automatic low preset on mobile: no water blur, no DOF, lower shadow-map resolution. The stated goal was smooth frame rates on all devices.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Colourful but coherent: define ProDevly's 6–8 brand colours as one palette texture (or uniform array) that every totem material samples. Ship an explicit mobile preset that turns off DOF and blur and halves shadow resolution.

sites.name: Active Theory V6 (studio site)
sites.award: Awwwards Site of the Month Feb 2024
sites.what_3d_does: Observed: a black screen with a HUD-style '/10' loader, then a holographic emblem (concentric lines around a hatched disc). Next, a dark teal volumetric environment full of drifting dust particles, where a glass ring holds the logo. Scrolling dives the camera: the ring turns edge-on and a light-trail ribbon loops below. Minimal pill nav (Work / Contact).
sites.palette_and_type: Near-black teal with cool light, tiny monospace HUD type.
sites.scroll_choreography: A continuous camera dive through one atmospheric space.
sites.takeaway_for_prodevly: Mostly a warning. The dark-space + particle-dust + glowing-logo-ring look is the most copied 'agency 3D' aesthetic and reads as generic. ProDevly should go light or coloured, with solid sculptural objects.

recurring_patterns: One hero object, many beats. Most winners pin a single sculptural object (Oryzo's coaster, Akaru's monolith, PX PUSH's chrome logo and floppy disk, Trionn's glass symbol) and map scroll to its pose: rotation, tilt, assembled ↔ exploded. They do not drag it across the screen, so the camera never has to chase anything.

Each site commits to one hero material that tells its story: ice (Igloo), cork (Oryzo), plaster bas-relief (Immersive Garden), chrome (PX PUSH), transmissive glass panels (Trionn), glossy plastic (Lusion), toon matte (Messenger).

Restrained palettes. Awwwards lists only 2 colours for most winners (Igloo, Kriss, Oryzo, Cerebrium, Shopify, PX PUSH, Messenger). 'Colourful' comes from one strong accent, or from a single shared palette texture as Bruno Simon does.
Physical → digital transformation as the narrative engine: Terminal's truck → wireframe twin, Oryzo's 3D → 2D → 3D, Shader's camera flying into a CRT screen to enter the next scene.

Architecture: one fixed canvas behind DOM text, a section config, only visible or adjacent scenes rendered or mounted, FBO-based scene-to-scene transitions, and scroll values written to uniforms through refs, not React state (Shader.se, Shopify, Cerebrium).

A single normalised state value per object, combining scroll, hover and press (Trionn's explodeAmt), so interactions blend, reverse and get interrupted smoothly. Damped (lerped) following rather than 1:1 scroll sync.
Hover interactions use raycasting against real geometry, with memory or decay: Cerebrium's shield remembers touches, Trionn's panels 'charge' and decay exponentially, Phantom's grid has inertia.
Rich loaders and intros (numeric counters, CAD reticles, HUDs) that hand off seamlessly into the scene. Some add synthesised Web Audio or a soundtrack (Igloo, Trionn, Zentry, Bruno).

Expressive typography paired with the 3D: giant condensed wordmarks (Akaru, Slosh), custom distorted faces (Zentry/FK Screamer), serif + condensed mixes (Lando), blur-to-sharp character reveals (Trionn).
Real, interactive numbers instead of marketing stats: Terminal's ROI calculator, Cerebrium's transparent pricing calculator, Akaru's real awards list.

Serious performance engineering: device tiers with a static fallback, DPR clamping, Draco and KTX2, worker decoding, render-on-demand, camera paths baked from C4D or Blender, preloading the next scene's FBO. WebGPU/TSL is trending, but a WebGL fallback is still essential (Cerebrium went back to WebGL over a 20 s shader compile).

Mobile is recomposed, not shrunk. Lusion turns the 3D card portrait. Oryzo centres the object and stacks copy above and below. PX PUSH switches to native scroll. Trionn uses gsap.matchMedia for separate values. Bruno and Shopify ship lower-quality presets.
cliches_to_avoid: Dark navy or black 'space' with floating particle dust and a glowing logo ring or orb: the most imitated agency-3D look, Active Theory's signature.
Purple-to-blue gradient blobs, mesh-gradient backgrounds and frosted glassmorphism cards on every surface.
Bento-grid feature cards with line icons, plus a row of fabricated counters ('500+ projects', '99% satisfaction', '10+ years'). Use real lists, real logos with permission, or interactive calculators.
Meaningless primitives (torus knots, icosahedrons, chrome blobs) with no link to the brand story. Every totem should stand for something specific to ProDevly (a service, the logo, a tech area).
Camera or object locked 1:1 to raw scroll, causing jitter and 'too fast to follow' motion. Use damped progress with a maximum velocity.
Desktop composition merely shrunk on mobile (3D stuck on one side, monotonous). Recompose: portrait card, object centred, copy stacked.
Heavy scroll-jacking, hidden navigation, or text and UI rendered inside the canvas. This hurts accessibility and SEO; keep copy in the DOM.
Overused post-processing: constant chromatic aberration, glitch, film grain and heavy bloom washing out the forms.
Long loaders (more than about 3–5 s), WebGPU-only builds with long shader compiles, many separate WebGL contexts (one per section), and big image sequences on phones.
Cursor-only interactions with no touch equivalent, and age, cookie or 'enter' gates placed in front of the hero.
Rainbow-everything colour. Use a defined palette (one palette texture or token set) with one or two hero accents per section.
Copying a famous winner's signature object one-to-one (Lusion's blue cross pile, Igloo's ice blocks, Lando's helmet reveal) instead of deriving forms from ProDevly's own brand.
